text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.69% today, continuing a strong two-week rally that has lifted the stock nearly 10% since early September. The gain reflects improving conditions for oil refiners: US crude has climbed to $107 per barrel, diesel and heating oil inventories remain tight at just 107.9 million barrels, and refineries are running at 96.8% capacity—near maximum utilization. These conditions allow refiners to earn wider margins by processing oil into fuel products that are in tight supply.

The broader backdrop has also turned supportive for the sector. While Middle East tensions have kept global crude prices elevated at $130.80 per barrel, the immediate supply fears have eased after Saudi Arabia signaled it would release additional crude following a pipeline attack, avoiding the worst-case disruption scenario. This combination of tight product supplies, high refinery utilization, and stable crude availability creates favorable economics for companies like Marathon that convert crude into gasoline and diesel.
